doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Trombonist at Youngstown clinic and J.J. playing Nutville
summary: A trombonist said fast lines can't be played on trombone; Aebersold lent him a J.J. Johnson cassette.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: That reminds me of a story. I was doing a clinic up at Youngstown, Ohio, probably thirty years ago, and I had some students playing the scales up to the ninth and back down and chords, and we may have played a blues or something. But it was rudimentary exercises. And I was packing up to leave ‘cause a guy was going to drive me back to Pittsburgh in order to fly back to Louisville and do this all in one day. And a gentleman walks up to me, he looked like he was about 33 years old, and he plays the trombone. He says, ”Jamey, playing those exercises is easy on the saxes and the trumpets and so forth but you can’t play that way on a trombone.” I said, “Oh you can’t?” He said, “No. Nobody plays like that on the trombone. Fast.” [scats] You know for instance. And I just happened to have a cassette of J.J. Johnson with Horace Silver and Woody Show and Joe Henderson in my — and I had a cassette player back then and I had that cassette. So I said, “Well here, you take this and play this first track over there.” And they were playing “Nutville.” Do you remember that tune?

“Nutville?” and J.J.’s solo is [scats] And I’m looking over at him and wondering what he’s thinking. And we didn’t really talk because I was busy packing up but I was thinking when I headed back to the airport, he’s got a decision to make. He’s going to start practicing or he’s going to give it up. Because the trombone can play that fast.
